## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components in an AoS layout can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Layout & approach
The 68 B/particle AoS offers loop 1 32 hot bytes (47%) — age+pos+seed+vel — and loop 2 28 (41%) — color+pos — leaving 53% and 59% dead weight per cacheline fill. No intermediates keeps the death verdict in registers but puts the branchy respawn inline with integration. The compiler must vectorize component-wise FP within stride-68B; sequential access is prefetch-friendly despite the low hot fraction. Working set spills from L1d at N≈963, from L2 at N≈61680.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p is flat at 3.6–3.9 across L1d (N=380–960), steps to 3.9–5.0 in L2 (N=1400–41000), then settles to 4.2–4.35 in DRAM (N=62000+). The L1d→L2 transition at N≈963 is gentle (3.84→3.92). The L2→DRAM spill at N≈62000 shows no penalty — ns/p drops from 4.47 to 4.25 as prefetch amortizes the sequential stride. The dense grid resolves the knee: cost is flat across DRAM. The 47% hot fraction wastes half each cacheline but creates no spill cliff because access remains streaming.

## Bandwidth
The floor is 2.274 ns/p; at q=0.01 the algo runs 3.6–4.35 ns/p (1.6–1.9x floor), so half the time is irreducible memory. Achieved bandwidth peaks at 18.73 GB/s (63% of the 29.9 ceiling) in L1d, settling to 15.6–16.2 GB/s (52–54%) in DRAM. At q=0.01 this algo is the winner at every N (1.0x) and 0.50–0.63x of naive. As death rate rises, bandwidth collapses to 11.4 (q=0.1), 8.2 (q=0.25), 6.0 GB/s (q=0.5). The transition is branch-bound — branch_flush climbs from 8.1% to 42–44% — and the algo falls to 1.89–2.08x of the halide winner at q=0.5, narrowing to 0.83x of naive.

## Assembly
Loop 1 achieves partial vectorization: 6 vector + 7 scalar FP ops per iter. `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` handle the 4-lane position update, `ext.16b` rearranges lanes, `ld1.s` gathers velocity — but age, seed, and respawn stay scalar. The branchy respawn (`b.ge` → `bl spawn`) carries 11 cond-branches per iter. Loop 2 is select-based (`csel` ×12) but byte-granular scatter (`strb` ×19, `ldrb` ×13) writes RGB one byte at a time. Only 9 of 294 insns are vector — partial vectorization explains the 52% ceiling; branchy respawn explains the collapse.

## Verdict
Partially holds. At q=0.01 the algo is the winner everywhere (1.0x) and 0.50–0.63x of naive, sustaining 15.6–18.7 GB/s (52–63% of ceiling) — auto-vectorization approaches streaming on death-free workloads, though the 47% hot fraction and 6 vector FP ops cap it at 1.9x the floor. At q≥0.25, refuted: branch_flush rises to 45–47% and the algo falls to 1.52–2.08x of the halide winner, which blends respawn instead of branching. The 11-branch respawn path with `bl spawn` breaks the hypothesis.
